stem: A hospitalized client with confirmed C. difficile infection has had no diarrhea since this morning. A plan is entered to discontinue contact precautions immediately. Which action should the nurse take?

options.A: Clarify the plan because CDC recommends maintaining contact precautions for at least 48 hours after diarrhea resolves, and facilities may continue them longer through hospitalization
options.B: Discontinue precautions immediately because C. difficile precautions end with the first formed stool
options.C: Continue precautions for life because a prior C. difficile infection permanently requires isolation
options.D: Use contact precautions only during toileting because transmission does not occur from the client's environment

rationale: CDC acute-care guidance updated in May 2026 recommends maintaining contact precautions for confirmed C. difficile infection for at least 48 hours after diarrhea has resolved, with longer continuation up to the duration of hospitalization in some settings. C. difficile spores can contaminate the environment, so precautions are not limited to toileting encounters.
educational_objective: Apply current CDC duration guidance for C. difficile contact precautions and question premature discontinuation.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
source_document_title: Clinical Guidance for C. diff Infection Prevention in Acute Care Facilities
source_locator: Isolate and initiate contact precautions — confirmed CDI: maintain contact precautions for at least 48 hours after diarrhea has resolved, or longer up to duration of hospitalization
source_claim_supported: Confirmed CDI requires contact precautions for at least 48 hours after diarrhea resolves, potentially longer through hospitalization.

correction_summary: Replaced vague facility-protocol wording with the explicit May 2026 CDC minimum duration and converted recall into a premature-discontinuation safety decision.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A matches current CDC guidance.
